{"id": "2cdf6d9a-57aa-4f6f-82a9-b1c787ad0fc5", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Yes, the storage never expires, but at your current volume it costs almost nothing.

**Setup**
- Bedrock invocation logs go only to CloudWatch Logs, in the log group `/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations`. There is no S3 destination, so there are no S3 lifecycle rules to check.
- The log group has no retention policy, so logs are kept forever.
- It's a Standard-class log group, created in mid-October.

**Size and growth**
- It currently stores about 124 MB (about 0.12 GB).
- Weekly ingestion has been uneven:

| Week starting | Ingested |
|---|---|
| Oct 10 | about 1 MB |
| Oct 17 | about 48 MB |
| Oct 24 | about 37 MB |
| Oct 31 | about 59 MB |
| Nov 7 | about 119 MB (peak) |
| Nov 14 | about 41 MB |
| Nov 21 (partial week) | about 6 MB |

**Cost, using us-east-1 list prices from memory, so please verify them**
- Storage costs about $0.03 per GB-month, so 124 MB is roughly $0.004 a month.
- Ingestion costs about $0.50 per GB. Everything so far (about 0.3 GB) cost around $0.15 in total.
- If you kept the peak week's rate for a full year, the log group would reach a few GB. That is still only cents to a few dimes per month in storage.

**Things to watch**
- Ingestion is the larger cost, not storage. A big increase in Bedrock traffic or prompt size would show up there first.
- Video data delivery is on. If you start using video models, payloads could get much larger.
- The logs contain full prompts and responses, because text delivery is on. Keeping them forever may matter for data retention or privacy policy, even though it's cheap.

I'd set a retention period on the log group, such as 30, 90 or 365 days, depending on your audit needs. That makes the storage bounded. I can make that change if you tell me the period you want. It needs your approval before it runs.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
